Backend: 13/13 pytest cases green in /app/backend/tests/test_iter18_script_approval.py covering PATCH /projects/{pid}/script (truncation to 600/120/400 chars, scene-count mismatch → 400, wrong-status → 400), POST /projects/{pid}/script/regenerate (allowed from awaiting_script_approval + error, rejected from ready/generating, no extra credit charge), POST /projects/{pid}/script/approve (flips to generating; 400 from ready/generating), cross-user isolation (404 for user B on user A's project), and refund of credit_cost when run_after_script_approval fails synthetically (seeded project with empty scenes[] → status=error, credits refunded by exactly credit_cost). Frontend (ProjectView /project/{id}): script-approval-panel renders with 'Step 1 of 3' header + 3 buttons (regen/edit/approve) + 3 draft-scene-{i} cards; edit mode exposes edit-narration-{i}, edit-subtitle-{i}, edit-image-prompt-{i}, script-edit-title, script-save-btn, script-cancel-btn; PATCH persists edits (verified via re-render and toast 'Script updated'); approve flips project to generating, dismounts script-approval-panel, mounts generating-panel with progress bar and stage chips; storyboard and script-text blocks are correctly HIDDEN while awaiting_script_approval and appear post-approval. Zero page-errors, zero unexpected console errors.
critical_code_review_comments: ProjectView.jsx polling interval uses `p?.status` in its dependency array which causes the interval to be torn down and re-created every time status flips. Functionally correct (polling only fires when status==='generating') but slightly wasteful; consider using a ref for status inside the interval callback.

PATCH /projects/{pid}/script silently coerces empty strings by falling back to base value: `(sc.get('narration') or base.get('narration') or '')[:600]` — if a user actually wants to CLEAR a subtitle/image_prompt to '', they cannot (empty string is falsy so it falls back to the original). Consider using `sc['narration'] if 'narration' in sc else base.get('narration','')` if intentional empty edits should be supported.

run_after_script_approval refunds credit_cost on ANY exception, including transient ones. If the frontend allows a retry (via /projects/{id}/generate again) after refund, the user could accidentally spend the credit twice. Consider marking the project as 'refunded' so credit deduction is idempotent per project.
server.py is 1803 lines — recommended to split guided-approval routes, admin routes, and pipeline runners into separate modules for maintainability.

regenerate_script does not reset scenes[]/script/title/hook fields before scheduling run_pipeline; if _generate_script errors, the stale draft remains until the bg task finishes. Minor UX inconsistency (user sees 'Rewriting your script…' toast but stale scenes may still show for a beat).
